title: Why Your AI UX Is Broken (and It's Not the Model's Fault) — Mike Christensen, Ably
talk_summary: Mike Christensen argues that direct HTTP/SSE streaming couples an agent's output stream to one client connection, breaking resumability, multi-device continuity, and live steering. He proposes a 'durable session' layer (pub/sub channels with persistence, sequence numbers, and bidirectional control) between agents and clients, so agents write events to a shared session and any client can subscribe, resume, or steer.

takeaways.technique: Durable session as shared event log between agents and consumers
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents write streamed events to a persistent, addressable, resumable channel instead of piping directly to a client; clients subscribe and replay from where they left off.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent to write events directly to the session without thinking about the health of the end client's connection

takeaways.technique: Decouple sub-agent progress from orchestrator proxying
takeaways.what_they_do: Sub-agents write granular progress directly to the shared session; the orchestrator only consumes final results, avoiding a dual role of orchestrating and relaying.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the orchestrator only cares about the final results from these sub-agents. It shouldn't need to worry about relaying granular progress.

takeaways.technique: Bidirectional control channel for in-flight work
takeaways.what_they_do: Use a two-way transport so a client can cancel or steer a running generation, instead of only closing the connection (which is ambiguous between cancel and resume).
takeaways.evidence_quote: resume and cancel are mutually exclusive when you're using SSE in particular

takeaways.technique: Single subscription point for multi-agent activity
takeaways.what_they_do: Clients subscribe to one session entity and see activity from all agents and other clients, rather than subscribing per agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: clients only need to subscribe to a single entity as well
